extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (cohomology of sheaves, Riemann–Roch, Serre duality)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook chapter section giving theorems, definitions, exercises and sample proofs about sheaf cohomology on schemes: Čech cohomology computations, vanishing theorems, base-change results, Riemann–Roch for curves, degree and nefness, and Serre duality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness may be checked locally
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactness of a sequence of sheaves may be checked locally: to show a complex of sheaves is exact it suffices to show it is exact after localizing on a cover by distinguished opens D(fi) with (f1,...,fr)=1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an affine cover so each distinguished open is contained in an affine open; exactness after localization (or on each member of the cover) implies global exactness. (Used in proof of general case of exactness of complex (18.2.4.1).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine morphism cohomology identification
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is an affine morphism and Y is quasicompact and separated (so X is too), then for a quasicoherent sheaf F on X there is a natural isomorphism Hi(Y, π_* F) ≅ Hi(X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute cohomology using an affine cover U of Y; π^{-1}(U) is an affine cover of X and the pushforward identifies sections on π^{-1}(U) with sections on U.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural map for pushforward under quasicompact separated morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicompact separated morphism π : X → Y and quasicoherent F on X (with Y quasicompact separated) there is a natural morphism Hi(Y, π_* F) → Hi(X, F); it is an isomorphism for i = 0 but need not be for higher i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example showing non-isomorphism for i=1: X = P1_k, F = O(−2), Y = Spec k; use this to be cautious about higher cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology commutes with filtered colimits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohomology commutes with filtered colimits: taking filtered colimits is an exact functor in the category of modules over a ring, so Hi(X, –) commutes with filtered colimits for quasicoherent sheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by hand or reduce to module case (hint uses exactness of filtered colimits in Mod_R). See Exercise 1.6.13 for module facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base change for field extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated k-scheme and F a quasicoherent sheaf, then for any field extension K/k there are natural isomorphisms Hi(X, F) ⊗_k K ≅ Hi(X ×_{Spec k} Spec K, F ⊗_k K) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lets one relate cohomology over k to cohomology over algebraically closed fields; proofs may use linear algebra (vector space) methods or the FHF theorem in more general flat situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-point-freeness is independent of extension of base field
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated k-scheme and L an invertible sheaf, then L is base-point-free iff its pullback to X ×_{Spec k} Spec K is base-point-free for any field extension K/k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exercise 18.2.H with i = 0: a basis of sections over k becomes a basis after tensoring with K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensional cohomology vanishing for projective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a projective k-scheme and F a quasicoherent sheaf on X, then Hi(X, F) = 0 for i > dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses covering by n+1 affine opens (for dim X = n) obtained from complements of effective Cartier divisors; more general versions use blowing up and derived functor machinery. This is a fundamental vanishing theorem used repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: General dimensional cohomology vanishing (Noetherian spaces)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a Noetherian topological space and F any sheaf of abelian groups, then Hi(X, F) = 0 for all i > dim X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grothendieck's proof sketched in references; applies to k-varieties (even pathological ones) to conclude cohomology vanishing above dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Čech cohomology computation for A^{n+1} minus origin
rubrics_metrics.description: For X = A^{n+1}_A  ackslash V(x0,...,xn) with cover by Ui = D(xi), Hi(X, O_X) = 0 unless i = 0 (where it is A[x0,...,xn]) or i = n (identified with certain Laurent polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the Čech complex, analyze multidegree (monomial) by monomial splitting into cases by number of negative exponents (0,1,2,...). Use exactness in each multidegree; for the top cohomology identify H^n with Laurent monomials having all exponents ≤ −1 except suitable degree constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy/id versus zero trick for proving exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: If one constructs an explicit homotopy between the identity map and the zero map of a complex, then the induced map on homology is zero, implying the homology groups are zero (so the complex is exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly (e.g., in 18.2.4.2 and 18.3.2.4) as an enlightening alternative to long exact sequence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler characteristic definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For a projective k-scheme X and coherent sheaf F, the Euler characteristic is χ(X, F) := Σ_{i=0}^{dim X} (−1)^i h^i(X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Euler characteristics behave better than individual cohomology groups and are often easier to compute; they are central to Riemann–Roch-type arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler characteristic is additive in exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F → G → H → 0 is an exact sequence of coherent sheaves on a projective k-scheme X, then χ(X, G) = χ(X, F) + χ(X, H). More generally alternating sums of χ over a short exact sequence filtration sum to zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the long exact sequence in cohomology to prove additivity; this property underlies many degree and Riemann–Roch computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riemann–Roch for line bundles on a projective curve (first version)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a divisor D on a projective (pure dimension 1) curve C over k, χ(C, O_C(D)) = deg D + χ(C, O_C). Equivalently for a line bundle L on a curve, h^0(C,L) − h^1(C,L) = deg L − pa(C) + 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by induction on degree using the exact sequence associated to adding a point divisor and additivity of χ. This is the central Riemann–Roch statement used in later exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a line bundle on a projective curve
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is an invertible sheaf on a projective curve C, define deg L := χ(C, L) − χ(C, O_C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition matches counting zeros and poles of rational sections for regular curves; it extends to coherent sheaves (with rank) via deg F = χ(C, F) − (rank F) χ(C, O_C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of a divisor equals degree of corresponding line bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is an invertible sheaf on a projective curve C and s is a nonzero rational section with divisor D = Σ v_p(s)[p], then deg L = deg D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the short exact sequence 0 → O_C(−p) → O_C → O|_p → 0 and additivity of Euler characteristic to relate degrees; choose sections not vanishing on components to compute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two global sections with no common zeros give finite morphism to P^1
rubrics_metrics.description: If s1 and s2 are two sections of a degree d line bundle L on an irreducible regular curve C with no common zeros, they determine a morphism π : C → P^1_k which is finite and of degree d.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the pair as a base-point-free 2-dimensional linear system; show π is finite and compute degree via pullback of O(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback degree under finite morphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : C → C' is a degree d morphism of integral projective regular curves and L is an invertible sheaf on C', then deg_C π^* L = d · deg_{C'} L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute using nonzero rational sections and how zeros/poles pull back; exercise 16.3.D may help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic genus definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For a dimension n scheme X, the arithmetic genus is pa(X) := (−1)^n(χ(X, O_X) − 1). For integral projective curves over algebraically closed fields, pa(C) = h^1(C, O_C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to rewrite Riemann–Roch in the familiar form h^0 − h^1 = deg L − pa + 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree for coherent sheaves / Riemann–Roch for sheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is projective and F a coherent sheaf of rank r on C, define deg F = χ(C, F) − (rank F) χ(C, O_C). This is often called Riemann–Roch for coherent sheaves (vector bundles) on a projective curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If F is torsion this recovers degree via length; degree is additive in short exact sequences of coherent sheaves on a fixed curve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical equivalence and Pic_τ subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on a proper k-variety X is numerically trivial if deg_C L = 0 for all one-dimensional closed reduced subschemes C (equivalently for all integral curves C). Numerically trivial line bundles form a subgroup Pic_τ X ⊂ Pic X; quotient by numerically trivial gives N1(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerical properties (like nefness and ampleness) depend only on the class in N1(X). Picard number ρ(X) is rank of N1(X) and is finitely generated (Néron–Severi theorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and basic properties of nef (numerically effective)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L is nef if deg_C L ≥ 0 for all integral curves C in X. Nefness is a numerical property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: (a) L nef iff it is nef on each irreducible component; (b) pullback of nef is nef; (c) tensor products of nef are nef; (d) ample ⇒ nef; (e) for n>0, L is nef iff L^{⊗n} is nef. Nef Q-line bundles form a closed cone in N1_Q(X).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample cone is interior of nef cone (Kleiman criterion context)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projective X, ampleness depends only on the class in N1(X); ample divisors form a cone in N1_Q(X) and are precisely the interior of the nef cone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph foreshadows Kleiman's numerical criterion for ampleness (Theorem 20.4.6). Use Exercise 16.2.H and properties of nefness to relate cones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre duality for smooth projective varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a geometrically irreducible smooth projective k-variety of dimension n, there is an invertible sheaf ω_X such that for all finite rank locally free sheaves F and all i, Hi(X, F) is dual to H^{n−i}(X, ω_X ⊗ F^∨), and there is a perfect pairing Hi(X, F) × H^{n−i}(X, ω_X ⊗ F^∨) → H^n(X, ω_X) ≅ k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ω_X is a dualizing sheaf (canonical sheaf); Serre duality can be realized via derived functors and perfect pairings. Smoothness can be relaxed; see later chapters for formal derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical sheaf as determinant of cotangent bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Serre-dualizing sheaf ω_X can be identified with the canonical sheaf K_X, defined as the determinant of the cotangent bundle Ω_{X/k} for smooth varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification will be justified later; the canonical bundle interpretation allows geometric understanding of Serre duality (see §30.4 and Desideratum 30.1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of vector bundles on P^1 (Grothendieck)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is a rank r vector bundle on P^1_k, then E ≅ ⊕_{i=1}^r O(a_i) for a unique nondecreasing sequence of integers a_1 ≤ ··· ≤ a_r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness of the splitting can be detected from dimensions dim_k Hom(O(m), E) as m ranges; existence is proved by induction on rank using cohomological arguments (Serre's Theorem A, vanishing, and possibly Serre duality), but there are also non-cohomological proofs.
